participants: Toyan (external sales coach and mentor; also a property investment consultant)
summary: A roughly 21-minute opening session of a private sales-mentorship programme in which Harry Edmonds is the paying student and Toyan is the external coach — no Primal Instinct business is discussed and no prospect is present. Toyan frames it as a first-session 'game plan' to assess how Harry communicates, then works through which of three closer phases Harry is in: building experience, maximising income, or optimising for alignment and work-life balance. He tests it with a forced choice between an eight-hour-day B2B offer paying 20k a month and a three-hour-day fitness offer paying 6k; Harry picks the higher-paying one, which Toyan reads as evidence Harry is not yet in the alignment phase he claims. The rest is a values conversation about ideal daily life, a shared plan to earn 15k a month while living on three or four, and Toyan pivoting into his property-investment business to argue Harry could reach £5,000 a month passive from £300,000 invested. The most consequential moment for this audit is the last exchange: Harry notices his Fathom notetaker is present, identifies it as belonging to his previous employer, and asks for it to be removed — which is why this private session exists in the Primal Instinct Drive folder at all.
notable: The rep has left the Primal Instinct offer. Toyan opens with 'this fitness offer that you used to be on, are you going back to that?' and Harry confirms in the past tense, and at 00:21:04 identifies the Fathom notetaker itself as belonging to 'my old offer'. The last sales call in this batch is 9 June; this is 15 June.

A stated lead-volume shortage is given as the reason he was not taken back: 'I spoke to my old manager. He said no, because they said they ain't got lead volume, but I'm going to try and get back on my old, old fitness offer.' If that refers to Primal Instinct it is a material pipeline fact; the transcript does not disambiguate between his two previous fitness offers, so it is recorded as stated rather than attributed.

This recording should never have entered the corpus. It is a private, paid coaching session between the rep and an unaffiliated third party, captured because the rep's Fathom notetaker was still bound to his former employer's account and filing into their Drive. Harry realised it mid-call — 'can you remove this Fathom? My Fathom, though. Because I just realized that this is from my old offer.'

Career and earnings history stated for the record: two and a half years closing, starting in B2B then moving to fitness; 'I made 10 grand in my third month' in 2024; has lived in 12 countries; target is 15k a month while living on three to four and saving the rest.

Toyan discloses his own figures and background: formerly Johnny Mao's sales manager doing 60k a month on 14-hour days, now running his own programme at a stated 100k a month; nearly 40 with five children; also a property investment consultant.

Toyan moves from mentorship into his other business inside the same session, telling a 22-year-old student that £300,000 invested in property 'if you did it in the right way' would yield £5,000 a month and that he could earn that sum in a year. Outside Primal Instinct's scope, but recorded because it is a coach cross-selling regulated-adjacent investment advice to a client he is mentoring on something else.

Names appearing that may recur elsewhere in the corpus: Bryan Ostermiller (described here as Cole Gordon's business partner and co-founder of Closers.io and RCA — the same coach as the 1 June session), Connor (a fellow student of Toyan's who Harry says he once helped close on a live call and who reportedly did 33k last month), Edward, Bogdan, Johnny Mao, Josh Lyons.

Recording disclosure was made by the external coach at the outset — 'This meeting is being recorded' — but neither party had consented to it landing in Primal Instinct's Drive, which is what actually happened.

Diarization is unreliable and inverts frequently on short turns; at 00:00:00, 00:01:39, 00:04:34 and 00:19:03 the speakers are crossed mid-exchange. Roles were read from content: Toyan is the coach, nearly 40, with five children and a property business; Harry is the 22-year-old student.
